result.stdout:
Description:
  Filestar: convert, resize, compress and edit files from the command line.

Usage:
  FilestarCli [command] [options]

Options:
  -i, --input <input> (REQUIRED)                      Input files - absolute, relative or pattern
  -o, --output <output>                               Output path
  -c, --command <command>                             Command, i.e. "convert to jpg"
  -p, --parameters <parameters>                       Skill parameters, one name:value per argument: -p Quality:80 Format:cube (or --Quality 80; 'filestarcli skills describe' lists them)
  -r, --recursive                                     Find files in subdirectories
  --output-template <output-template>                 Output path template, i.e. "<Filename>.<Extension>"
  --loglevel <Headless|Normal|Quiet|Verbose>          Log level [default: Normal]
  --recipe <recipe>                                   Path to recipe file
  --cloud <Allowed|Disallowed|Forced>                 Cloud policy (Disallowed keeps every file on this computer) [default: Allowed]
  --output-conflict <AppendNumber|Replace|Skip|Warn>  Strategy to use if there are conflicting filenames [default: AppendNumber]
  --progress <json>                                   Progress format: json writes NDJSON events to stderr
  --parameters-json <json>                            Skill parameters as one JSON object, e.g. '{"Quality":80}' (same as -p)
  --dry-run                                           Show which skill(s) would run, with which parameters, local or cloud; run nothing
  --output-dir <folder>                               Folder to write the outputs to (created if missing)
  --overwrite                                         Replace existing files with the same name (default: never overwrite, add a number)
  --timeout <duration>                                Stop after this long: seconds, or 90s, 5m, 1h (exit 7, half-written outputs removed)
  --json                                              Write one JSON document to stdout (messages go to stderr).

Description:
  Print the file type Filestar decides for each file, and why. Nothing is converted.

Usage:
  FilestarCli detect [<path>...] [options]

Arguments:
  <path>  Files, folders or patterns (*.png)

Options:
  -r, --recursive              With a folder or pattern, include subfolders
  --no-extension               Decide as if the file had no extension (by content only)
  --candidates                 Also list every type that was scored, best first
  -?, -h, --help               Show help and usage information
  --json                       Write one JSON document to stdout (messages go to stderr).
  --user-agent <name/version>  Who is running Filestar, e.g. "claude-code/2.1" (else FILESTAR_USER_AGENT, else a guess).

Examples:
  filestarcli detect photo.heic
  filestarcli detect ./downloads -r --json
